raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County on 12 mu with a wheat-maize rotation, and I have well irrigation, so I will keep the full 12 mu in the same system this year. I have been farming a long time, so I will stay with the kind of practices that are familiar, reliable, and manageable for my family, especially because some family members work off-farm and I need a plan that is steady rather than complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer on at planting with a topdressing of nitrogen later, irrigate at key stages, and keep tillage moderate with rotary tillage because it is practical and fits my conditions. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield, apply enough nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and potassium, irrigate when rain is not enough, and continue rotary tillage so field preparation stays simple. I will not push inputs to extremes; I will aim for stable production, protect the crop with a limited number of pesticide sprays, and rely on irrigation and familiar field management to reduce risk.
